title: Scheduling an expiration date
question: Q5
take: Video share panel: expiry with quick presets (24h / 1 week / 2 weeks) plus exact date+time, passphrase toggle, and the resulting expiry shown inline as 'Dec 31 at 11:59pm' with Edit.

title: Editing share settings
question: Q5
take: Separate 'Link for editing' vs 'Link for viewing' tabs, each with its own expiration toggle+date, password and download controls; 'Restrictions apply - Modify' surfaces the constraint next to Copy link; 'Unshare file' as the revoke-all action.

title: Adding expiration date
question: Q5
take: Publish-to-web popover lists Password / Email access / Expiration as one stack of settings with 'Never' defaults; calendar offers 'Expire on Thu, Apr 30' vs 'Never expires'; a single Unpublish button revokes, and a viewer count shows who actually used the link.

title: Updating link access
question: Q5
take: 'Visitor link access' is a distinct tier for people WITHOUT an account (anonymous learners): its own view/no-access level, optional password, expiration date shown as 'Expires Feb 28, 2025, 10:50 AM GMT-7', and 'Reset visitor link' to revoke by rotating the URL without touching workspace members.

title: Updating content status
question: Q5
take: Course lessons carry a Draft / Published / Scheduled / Public preview status badge with a date; multi-select lessons and 'Set status for 2 selected' in bulk - the closest analogue to faculty releasing recordings on a date.

title: Scheduling a post
question: Q5
take: Publish step as a plain-language sentence ('Set it live now' vs 'Schedule for later' + date/time), then a confirmation 'Your post will be published on October 25th at 01:42' with a one-click 'Unschedule and revert to draft' undo.

title: Sharing settings - share the link with
question: Q5
take: The OneDrive/SharePoint model the customer asked for: audience radio (Anyone / People you choose / People with existing access), then Can edit level, expiry date field, 'Require verification' and 'Set password' in one compact sheet.

title: Proton Drive public link settings
question: Q5
take: Revocation written as a consequence, not a verb: 'Stop sharing - erase this link and remove everyone with access', sitting under expiration date and link password toggles.

title: View-only link panel
question: Q5
take: View-only link explicitly framed as 'allows anyone to see the file, no sign-in required', with a LIVE badge, preview of what recipients will see, password toggle and Delete link / Update link.

title: Share link to board - settings
question: Q5
take: Security tier for media links: 'Require name and email to view' (lightweight identification without an account), passcode, expiration date - each an independent toggle.

title: Share settings
question: Q5
take: Link settings decomposed into three questions - Who can access / What can they do (View vs Edit) / Additional security - and a note that link settings do not override people already invited directly.

title: Who can access - per-person access with Remove
question: Q5
take: Access list shows inherited access ('People with access to Team Folder') separately from direct grants; each direct person has a Can view dropdown with Remove inline and an 'Outside your team' label.

title: Sharing a file (NordLocker)
question: Q5
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: terms checkbox before generating a link, a separate security code the sender must transmit out-of-band, fixed expiry you cannot change, link frozen to one file version - security that pushes work onto the sharer.

title: Generating a share link
question: Q5
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE (with one keeper): per-field permission checklist and 1-hour default expiry are overkill for training content, but the live '59 mins' countdown ring on the published-link screen is a good way to make a time-box visible.

title: Logging in (magic link)
question: Q6
take: Work-email-only sign in, no password field exists; after sending the link it offers 'Open your email client: Gmail / Outlook / Superhuman' buttons to close the loop in one click.

title: Logging in (magic link)
question: Q6
take: 'Sign in with email' as one of several login options; confirmation screen with 'Go to inbox' and an always-visible 'Back to login options' escape so a user never gets stuck on a method.

title: Logging In (Google / Microsoft / magic link)
question: Q6
take: Three equal-weight buttons (Continue with Google / Microsoft / email) with 'Remember me for 28 days' so occasional users (faculty) rarely see login at all; email path is a magic link, and the wait screen shows who you are signing in as with a logout link.

title: Logging In (email or Google, no password)
question: Q6
take: Minimal 'plug and play' entry: one Google button and one email field - there is no password to forget, no sign-up vs sign-in split, and 'Check your inbox' offers only Resend.

title: Logging in (6-digit email code)
question: Q6
take: One-time code instead of a link (works when the email client is on another device); 'Use a different email' and a yellow nudge 'still waiting on your code? try signing up instead' handle the no-account case without a dead end.

title: Logging in with passcode
question: Q6
take: The 'forgot password' link is rewritten as 'Forgot password? Log in with passcode' - the recovery path IS a login path (emailed code), so a forgotten password never blocks the session or requires a reset.

title: Resetting password (with one-time code escape hatch)
question: Q6
take: On 'Incorrect email address or password' the same screen offers 'Log in with a one-time code' as an OR path, and the reset itself is a 6-digit emailed code rather than a link.

title: Logging in (email code, 'Last used' badge)
question: Q6
take: A 'Last used' badge on the sign-in method you picked last time (email vs Google vs Microsoft) - removes the 'which account did I use?' guess that causes duplicate accounts and lockouts.

title: Sign in with Google / Microsoft / LinkedIn / SSO / instant link
question: Q6
take: One screen offers every institutional path - Google, Microsoft, SSO - AND 'Email me a link to sign in instantly' as a peer of the password button, so a locked-out user has three ways in without support.

title: Too many login attempts - login with code
question: Q6
take: Rate-limit dialog offers 'Login with code' as the primary way out instead of a hard lockout - the direct antidote to months-long password lockouts.

title: Incorrect password - send a code instead
question: Q6
take: Microsoft account (the institution's own IdP): wrong password shows 'Send a code to <email>' inline under Next - relevant because hospital/university users already live in this pattern.

title: Security settings - passkey recommended, secondary email
question: Q6
take: Security page ranks Passkeys 'Recommended' above Password, explains 'takes under a minute', and adds 'Secondary email - used to restore access' so recovery does not depend on one institutional mailbox.

title: Post-login prompt - add passkey
question: Q6
take: 'Log in faster next time' banner shown right after a successful login - the moment to offer a passkey - with a dismiss X, never a blocking step.

title: Create a passkey
question: Q6
take: Passkey modal explains in plain words what you will log in with (Face ID / Touch ID / Passcode); Security page also lists Recovery phone as a backup channel and current login activity.

title: Resetting password
question: Q6
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: vague 'Unable to verify your account' error, only exit is Forgot password -> emailed reset link -> new password -> log in again; the whole session depends on the recovery email working.

title: Recover your account with recovery key
question: Q6
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: recovery depends on a key PDF saved on 'the device you used to sign up' - exactly the hidden recovery dependency that produces six-month lockouts; failure message gives no alternative.

title: Recover Account - link invalid or expired
question: Q6
take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE of the expired-link dead end: 'link you followed is invalid, or it has expired' with only a text 'try again' - shows why magic links need a code fallback and a visible expiry.
